conventions.convention: Fields on T^d are represented by 2π-periodic lifts; spatial integration means Lebesgue integration over Q_d=[0,2π]^d. Time-space integration is iterated with space first. Countable Choice AC_ω is assumed for the measure and integration suppliers.
The stratified branch has constant f∈R, N>0 and ν,κ≥0, with vertical forcing +b e_3 and buoyancy equation b_t+N²u_3=κΔb. The inviscid branch sets ν=κ=0.

The rotation convention is e_3×u=(-u_2,u_1,0) and Jv=(-v_2,v_1). A positively rotating basis satisfies its angular-velocity differential equation; f=2Ω places the Coriolis term on the left with positive sign. Tensor divergence is rowwise.
The shallow-water branch has positive depth, constant g>0 and f∈R, one layer, fixed flat bottom and no friction. Its energy density per reference density is h|v|²/2+gh²/2.

These are mathematical equation families with prescribed coefficients, not measured fluid states or empirical validity claims. Energy integrals omit constant reference mass density; multiplying by that density gives joules under the stated SI interpretation.

load_bearing.statement: On T³ the classical periodic stratified family is u_t+f e_3×u+∇π=b e_3+νΔu, ∇·u=0, b_t+N²u_3=κΔb, with constant f∈R, N>0 and ν,κ≥0. Independently, on T² the positive-depth shallow-water family is h_t+∇·(hv)=0 and (hv)_t+∇·(hv⊗v)+∇(gh²/2)+fhJv=0, with constant g>0 and f∈R, fixed flat bottom and no friction.

Assume AC_ω. For the stated periodic stratified equations with constant f∈R, N>0 and ν,κ≥0, u,b continuously differentiable in time and space with continuous second spatial derivatives, and π having continuous first spatial derivatives, E(t)=½∫Q₃(|u|²+b²/N²) dx satisfies E(t₁)-E(t₀)=-∫t₀^t₁∫Q₃(ν|∇u|²+κ|∇b|²/N²) dx dt for every t₀<t₁ in I. Consequently E is conserved in the inviscid branch and otherwise nonincreasing.

Assume AC_ω. For the stated positive-depth, smooth periodic, flat-bottom inviscid shallow-water solutions with constant f∈R and g>0, E=h|v|²/2+gh²/2 satisfies ∂_tE+∇·((E+gh²/2)v)=0 pointwise, and its integral over Q₂ is conserved.

concerns.concern: The Statement requires only that π have continuous first spatial derivatives. Facts [A1] nevertheless says that 'every product and derivative below is continuous on each compact time interval times Q_3', and Proof 3.1 integrates individual spatial flux derivatives over the time-space rectangle. The pressure hypothesis permits π(t,x)=c(t) with arbitrary discontinuous c. For example, take f=ν=κ=0, b=0 and the stationary divergence-free field u=(sin(x₁)cos(x₂),-cos(x₁)sin(x₂),0), with c(t) the indicator of rational times. All displayed equations hold and ∇π=0 is continuous, but the individual derivatives ∂₁(πu₁) and ∂₂(πu₂) are not Riemann integrable on time-space rectangles. Their sum vanishes, so the energy claim remains sound. The proof needs an explicit pressure-gauge normalization, such as subtracting π(t,0), or a spatial-slice cancellation argument that avoids the unsupported individual time-space integrals.
